BOUNDARY: The hypothesis \(n \ge 1\) is explicit; the sequence range is nonempty, so boundedness supplies a centre \(q\) and \(r>0\).  Then \(M=r+\lVert q\rVert_2>0\) yields a non‑degenerate box, which is compact by the Heine‑Borel clause for closed boxes.  Compactness implies sequential compactness without any choice (via the cited ZF theorem).  Convergence in the subspace transfers to the ambient Euclidean metric because the subspace metric is the restriction.  Norm equivalence gives the claimed generalisation to arbitrary norms as a consequence.
